summary: Haaretz reported that Ben-Gvir used an Israel Police helicopter to travel from a private northern vacation to public events in central Israel and back toward his vacation; the same police-volunteer event had been permitted only after his sworn commitment not to campaign there.
notes: Concrete public-resource-use lead. Zman Israel independently preserves the Haaretz report and says aviation professionals estimated the flights at tens of thousands of shekels. Justice Noam Sohlberg separately allowed Ben-Gvir to speak at the Aug. 24 police event after a sworn undertaking not to campaign. No formal post-event Elections Committee finding establishing a breach and no sufficiently complete official helicopter authorization/response record were recovered. Keep Pending; do not infer illegality, self-interest or misuse beyond documented facts.

summary: During/after Ben-Gvir's filmed visit to Palestinian women prisoners at Damon Prison, the Public Committee Against Torture in Israel asked the Central Elections Committee chair to order the video removed and to bar further publicized prison visits through the election period.
notes: Fresh legal/ethical lead only. Walla reports the NGO petition alleged prohibited election propaganda/state-resource use and degrading treatment; this run did not recover an Elections Committee ruling on the Damon video. Walla also notes a separate earlier 2026 campaign-video matter in which Justice Noam Sohlberg ordered removal and imposed costs, but that prior ruling is not treated as an adjudication of this Damon incident. Keep Pending; preserve Ben-Gvir's conduct/video as reported but do not label the Damon visit illegal or an established campaign breach absent a ruling or stronger official finding.
